comparisons.peer_topic: Long-Term Debt Maturities and Buyback Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: Total long-term debt decreased by $18.9 billion to $283.3 billion in 2024 due to maturities and redemptions, partially offset by new issuances and valuation adjustments, with the company retaining the option to purchase outstanding debt instruments based on market conditions and liquidity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America disclose active liability management strategies involving the redemption and repurchase of long-term debt to manage their balance sheets. Citi specifically quantified its activity, stating it redeemed or repurchased an aggregate of $46.8 billion of outstanding long-term debt in 2024 to reduce funding costs. Similarly, Bank of America reported that its long-term debt decreased by $18.9 billion in 2024, a change primarily driven by maturities and redemptions. While Citi highlights the strategic option to purchase debt based on market conditions, BAC explicitly confirms this discretionary approach, stating it may purchase outstanding debt instruments in various transactions depending on market conditions and liquidity.

sentences.text: As part of its liability management, Citi has considered, and may continue to consider, opportunities to redeem or repurchase its long-term debt pursuant to open market purchases, tender offers or other means.
During 2024, Citi redeemed or repurchased an aggregate of $46.8 billion of its outstanding long-term debt.
Total long-term debt decreased $18.9 billion to $283.3 billion during 2024, primarily due to maturities and redemptions, partially offset by debt issuances and valuation adjustments.
We may, from time to time, purchase outstanding debt instruments in various transactions, depending on market conditions, liquidity and other factors.
